Alex —

Thanks for sending over the redlines. To confirm Carebridge’s requirements at a summary level:

- We need an explicit, contract-level commitment that Redwood will not use Carebridge tenant data to train models or to improve model weights/parameters. Wording should cover both automated training and human-in-the-loop improvement workflows.
- For US patient data, we require onshore key management (customer-controlled KMS or an onshore HSM option) and assurance that backups/replicas will remain within the US region.
- For EU customers, we expect data residency in the EU region and that any subprocessor transfers are covered by adequate safeguards.
- We also require an inventory of subprocessors with a link to each subprocessor’s SOC2/ISO attestation if available, plus a simple evidence pack for any that access plaintext data.

I have attached our procurement checklist and the completed subprocessor intake form — that should make it easier to crosswalk against your inventory. For the no-training clause, procurement prefers a stand-alone clause rather than a sentence buried in a general data use section.

Next: please have your legal team provide a proposed stand-alone clause and ops to produce a short note describing per-tenant routing and KMS options (including whether you can support customer-managed keys). We’re on a tight compliance timeline for our pilot (targeting production in Q4), so the faster we can align on language + proof points, the better.

Regards,
Samantha Reyes
Head of Procurement | Carebridge Health

Alex / team —

Thanks for the context and the procurement checklist. Quick legal ops plan & proposed draft clause below. I kept it intentionally operationally-aware and limited in scope to what Carebridge requested so we don’t overpromise.

Proposed stand-alone clause (suggested DPA section titled "Model Improvement and Use of Customer Data"):
"Redwood Inference shall not use, incorporate, or otherwise process Customer Data to train, improve, refine, or modify any machine learning model weights, parameters, or configurations used by Redwood or any third party for the purpose of model improvement, benchmarking, or derivative model creation. This restriction applies to both automated training pipelines and human-in-the-loop review processes. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry that does not contain Customer Data or any data reasonably capable of re-identifying Customer Data for service monitoring and performance optimization, provided such telemetry cannot be used to reconstruct Customer Data."

Operational commitments to accompany clause (for insertion into schedule/ops addendum):
- Per-tenant routing: Redwood will map tenant identifiers to routing profiles. Carebridge's US customer tenants will be mapped to the onshore pool; EU customer tenants will be routed to EU-resident pools.
- Key management: Redwood can support customer-provided KMS keys via a customer key binding option (subject to onboarding and supported providers). If customer-managed keys are not provided, Redwood offers an onshore key management option for US-regional tenants.
- Subprocessor evidence: Redwood will provide a current subprocessor inventory plus links to SOC2/ISO attestations where available. For subprocessors with plaintext access, Redwood will provide a one-time evidence pack (architecture diagram + access controls + SOC2 excerpt). Future requests can be handled via quarterly attestations or a defined evidence meeting.

Ops ask to Dev: please confirm feasibility and provide an estimated timeline and effort (low/med/high) for: (a) KMS customer-key onboarding for a single Carebridge tenant, (b) mapping and enforcing tenant-level routing, and (c) producing the subprocessor evidence pack.

If ops confirms feasibility, I recommend we:
1) Insert the stand-alone clause into the DPA redlines and send to Carebridge legal.
2) Provide the evidence pack and our SOC2 link (https://redwood.com/security/soc2) in parallel.
3) Open a small implementation workstream with product ops + security to scope onboarding and timeline.

I’m copying Laura for any contractual nuance; Laura, flag anything that risks overcommitment.

—Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
